chapter: New York and the Himber years
title: Horace Diaz in New York; Hirsch as manager dealing with publishers and Glenn Miller
summary: Hirsch describes Diaz with Eddie Duchin, then his own New York job setting up broadcasts, talking to Glenn Miller weekly.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: He, uh, was he, I got the, I was with Horace and he was a good friend of Franzella's up in New York. And we used to go fishing. Mm-hmm. He sounded like I'd rather go fishing than eat. And we'd go out there and fish and we'd go fishing and spend the days together. And Horace was, uh, he was, in New York he was like, uh, Eddie, he was the second piano for Eddie Duchin. He played piano with Eddie Duchin's orchestra. And, uh, he is also an arranger for a southern music company. He made a lot of Horace Diaz. They had a lot of, a lot of Latin tunes when Latin first came out. He did a lot of Latin arrangements for southern music. Because I, I knew that, the, the professional manager up there. You see, I was in a position up there to know every professional manager in the business. Because I was him as manager. And we did all the broadcasting. Oh, really?

And I'd set up all the broadcasting acts with him as assistants. And, uh, in fact, I used to speak to Glenn Miller on an average of two to three times a week. Finding out, you see, in those days in, in radio, network radio, they were paid a royalty fee for the compositions. And, uh, the publisher, and the publisher, and the composer was, was getting a royalty. And, uh, that was on, on, on, on, on remotes. Remotes over, remotes over, uh, uh, networks. In other words, it was CBS, NBC, and ABC. It was, actually not, they're not, it wasn't ABC as yet, it was W.O.R. W.O.R. was, was ABC. And, uh, I'd ring up Glenn, and what are you gonna do this week? You know, well, you wanna do Sunday in New York, or you wanna do, blah, blah, blah, or, it isn't fair? And, that was Hymnless Compositions. Monday in New York, and It Isn't Fair, and a couple of other things that he wrote. And, uh, yeah. Well, I said, well, what do you want me to do? He said, well, do a serenade, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, you know, the sunrise serenade, or some shit like that. I can't remember the name of the title of it. And we talked every week, and that's, this is the way that these publishers, in fact, Hymnlessed me one time, that if I ever do a tune on the air for a kickback, he says, I'll fire you right now. He wouldn't allow me to take a dime or a dinner, or a lunch from even any one of these guys. And I didn't. There was one guy that, he was ready to commit suicide. I told him, I said, go ahead and kill yourself, I can't do a fucking thing for you.
